# Setup {#sec-setup}

```{r}
#| label: setup
start_time <- Sys.time()

options(width = 80)

p_required <- c(
  "tidyverse", # data wrangling
  "here", # relative paths
  "future", # parallel backend
  "furrr", # parallel map() functions
  "janitor", # tabyl
  "sessioninfo" # session info
)
packages <- rownames(installed.packages())
p_to_install <- p_required[!(p_required %in% packages)]
if (length(p_to_install) > 0) {
  install.packages(p_to_install)
}
sapply(p_required, require, character.only = TRUE)
rm(p_required, p_to_install, packages)
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data
# stacked waves ----------------------------------------------------------------
df_stacked <- read_rds(
  here(
    "data",
    "02_processed",
    "waves_stacked.rds"
  )
)

# load wording map
wording_map <- read_csv(
  here(
    "data",
    "02_processed",
    "question_wording_map.csv"
  )
)
```

# Recode Variable Values (Phase 8) {#sec-recode}

```{r}
#| label: collect-information
# colnames and current type ----------------------------------------------------
cols <- tibble(
  cols = df_stacked |> colnames(),
  col_type = df_stacked |> map_chr(class)
)
# pre-split by country — workers receive slices, not full df ------------------
countries <- df_stacked |> distinct(meta_country) |> pull(meta_country)
df_by_country <- countries |>
  set_names() |>
  lapply(function(country) filter(df_stacked, meta_country == country))
col_names <- names(df_stacked) # small vector, fine to export
compute_groups <- function(df_country) {
  cat(paste0("starting\n"))
  # signatures in one pass -----------------------------------------------------
  signatures <- sapply(seq_len(ncol(df_country)), function(i) {
    df_country[[i]] |>
      as.character() |>
      unique() |>
      sort() |>
      paste(collapse = "||")
  })
  # group + name back ----------------------------------------------------------
  groups <- split(seq_along(signatures), signatures)
  lapply(groups, function(idx) col_names[idx])
}
# run in parallel for each country --------------------------------------------
plan(multisession)
groups_named <- future_map(df_by_country, compute_groups)
plan(sequential)
```

```{r}
#| label: rm-collect-information
rm(cols, df_by_country, col_names, compute_groups, groups_named)
```

## Meta Variables {#sec-meta}

```{r}
#| label: recode-meta
df_stacked_recoded <- df_stacked |>
  mutate(
    # META VARS ----------------------------------------------------------------
    meta_wave = as.integer(meta_wave),
    # meta_country = ,
    meta_startdate = as.POSIXct(meta_startdate),
    meta_enddate = as.POSIXct(meta_enddate),
    # meta_status = ,
    # meta_ipaddress = ,
    meta_progress = as.integer(meta_progress),
    meta_duration_s = as.integer(meta_duration_s),
    meta_finished = as.logical(meta_finished),
    meta_recordeddate = as.POSIXct(meta_recordeddate),
    # meta_responseid = ,
    # meta_recipient_lastname = ,
    # meta_recipient_firstname = ,
    # meta_recipient_email = ,
    # meta_external_ref = ,
    meta_latitude = as.numeric(meta_latitude),
    meta_longitude = as.numeric(meta_longitude),
    # meta_distchannel = ,
    # meta_lang = ,
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: recode-gender
df_stacked_recoded <- df_stacked_recoded |>
  mutate(
    # GENDER -------------------------------------------------------------------
    q_gender = case_when(
      q_gender_raw %in% male_vec ~ "male",
      q_gender_raw %in% female_vec ~ "female",
      !is.na(q_gender_raw) ~ "other"
    ),
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: validate-gender-recode
df_stacked_recoded |>
  select(q_gender, q_gender_raw) |>
  filter(is.na(q_gender) & !is.na(q_gender_raw)) |>
  distinct(q_gender_raw)
```

```{r}
#| label: rm-gender
rm(male_vec, female_vec)
```

## Age {#sec-age}

```{r}
#| label: recode-age
df_stacked_recoded <- df_stacked_recoded |>
  mutate(
    # AGE ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    q_age = as.integer(str_extract(q_age_raw, "\\d+")),
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: validate-age-recode
df_stacked_recoded |>
  select(q_age, q_age_raw) |>
  filter(is.na(q_age) & !is.na(q_age_raw)) |>
  distinct(q_age_raw)
```

```{r}
nat_lookup <- c(
  setNames(rep("Austria", length(austria_vec)), austria_vec),

    rep("United Kingdom", length(united_kingdom_vec)),
    united_kingdom_vec
  ),
  setNames(rep("Other", length(other_country_vec)), other_country_vec)
)

# Translate tokens via lookup
translate_nat <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x)) {
    return(NA_character_)
  }
  tokens <- str_trim(str_split(x, ",")[[1]])
  translated <- nat_lookup[tokens]
  # keep original token if not found
  translated[is.na(translated)] <- tokens[is.na(translated)]
  paste(translated, collapse = ", ")
}
```

```{r}
  mutate(

    q_nationality = map_chr(q_nationality_raw, translate_nat),
```

## Attention Checks

### Recoding Logic: Attention Check Validation

The primary attention check variable (`der_att_check_3`) was decomposed into two distinct operational conditions to isolate logic errors and data quality issues. 

- **Condition 1 (`der_att_check_1`):** Validates response conformity. Evaluates to `TRUE` if the raw categorical input (`q_attn_check_raw`) matches an expected value within the predefined vector `other_vec`.
- **Condition 2 (`der_att_check_2`):** Validates data completeness. Evaluates to `TRUE` if the open-ended text string (`q_attn_check_text_raw`) contains data (`!is.na`).
- **Composite Variable (`der_att_check_3`):** Evaluates to `TRUE` if and only if both individual criteria are simultaneously satisfied (`der_att_check_1 & der_att_check_2`). 

This structural separation isolates respondents who selected the correct baseline categorical option but failed to provide the mandatory qualitative verification text (Condition 1 passed, Condition 2 failed), ensuring strict adherence to the validation criteria before data exclusion.

```{r}
# create logical pass/fail variable

df_stacked_recoded <- df_stacked_recoded |>
  mutate(
    der_att_check_1 = if_else(q_attn_check_raw %in% other_vec, TRUE, FALSE),
    der_att_check_2 = if_else(!is.na(q_attn_check_text_raw), TRUE, FALSE),
    der_att_check_3 = if_else(der_att_check_1 & der_att_check_2, TRUE, FALSE)
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: attention-check-validate

  count(der_att_check_1, der_att_check_2, der_att_check_3)

# 2. Results by group
df_stacked_recoded |>
  group_by(meta_country, meta_wave) |>
  count(der_att_check_3) |>
  print(n = 150)

# 3. Inspect failed raw
df_stacked_recoded |>
  filter(!der_att_check_1 & !is.na(q_attn_check_raw)) |>
  distinct(q_attn_check_raw) |>
  print(n = 100)

# 4. Inspect missing text
df_stacked_recoded |>
  filter(der_att_check_1 & !der_att_check_2) |>
  distinct(q_attn_check_raw, q_attn_check_text_raw)
```

```{r}
    ),
```

## CJEU Abolish and Satis Questions

```{r}
#| label: value-labels-cjeu-abolis-satis
# helper print loop for visual inspection
for (i in 1:length(countries)) {
  df_stacked |>
    filter(meta_country == countries[i]) |>
    distinct(q_cjeu_abolish_raw) |>
    print()
}

# code to computationally check differences in values
abolish_vals <- map(
  countries,
  ~ df_stacked |>
    filter(meta_country == .x) |>
    distinct(q_cjeu_abolish_raw) |>
    pull()
) |>
  setNames(countries)

satisf_vals <- map(
  countries,
  ~ df_stacked |>
    filter(meta_country == .x) |>
    distinct(q_cjeu_satisfaction_raw) |>
    pull()
) |>
  setNames(countries)

# TRUE if all countries share identical distinct values
identical(map(abolish_vals, sort), map(satisf_vals, sort))

# print values present in one but not other
map(
  countries,
  ~ {
    a <- abolish_vals[[.x]]
    s <- satisf_vals[[.x]]
    diff <- list(
      in_satisf_not_abolish = setdiff(s, a),
      in_abolish_not_satisf = setdiff(a, s)
    )
    if (any(lengths(diff) > 0)) list(country = .x, diff = diff)
  }
) |>
  compact()
# only concerns 8, 10, 11 (so scale errors)
# hence I can use 7scale agree disagree items

rm(
  abolish_vals,
  satisf_vals
)
```

```{r}
      .default = NA
    ),
    q_cjeu_satisfaction = case_when(
      q_cjeu_satisfaction_raw %in% strongly_disagree_vec ~ 1L,
      q_cjeu_satisfaction_raw %in% disagree_vec ~ 2L,
      q_cjeu_satisfaction_raw %in% somewhat_disagree_vec ~ 3L,

      q_cjeu_satisfaction_raw %in% agree_vec ~ 6L,
      q_cjeu_satisfaction_raw %in% strongly_agree_vec ~ 7L,
      .default = NA
    )
  )
```

## Political Interest and Nativism

The code below checks if existing 7scale agree/disagree value vectors cover the values of the political interest and nativism variables. It does so by collecting all distinct values country by country and then printing values not present in the lookup vectors. If only `NA` is printed, it means all values are covered.

```{r}
#| label: values-pol-interst-nativism
# nat int ----------------------------------------------------------------------
tmp <- tibble()

for (i in 1:length(countries)) {
  tmp <- tmp |>
    bind_rows(
      df_stacked |>
        filter(meta_country == countries[i]) |>
        distinct(q_nat_int_raw)
    )
}

tmp |>
  filter(
    !(q_nat_int_raw %in%
      c(
        strongly_disagree_vec,
        disagree_vec,
        somewhat_disagree_vec,
```

```{r}
    q_occ_current = case_when(
      q_occ_current_raw %in% farmer_vec ~ "farmer",
      q_occ_current_raw %in% fisherman_vec ~ "fisher",
      q_occ_current_raw %in% student_vec ~ "student",
      q_occ_current_raw %in% retired_ill_vec ~ "retired",
      q_occ_current_raw %in% unemployed_vec ~ "unemployed",
      q_occ_current_raw %in% homemaker_vec ~ "homemaker",
      q_occ_current_raw %in% skilled_manual_vec ~ "manual_skill",
      q_occ_current_raw %in% unskilled_manual_vec ~ "manual_unskill",
      q_occ_current_raw %in% supervisor_vec ~ "supervisor",
      q_occ_current_raw %in% desk_employee_vec ~ "emp_desk",
      q_occ_current_raw %in% service_employee_vec ~ "emp_service",
      q_occ_current_raw %in% travelling_employee_vec ~ "emp_travel",
      q_occ_current_raw %in% middle_management_vec ~ "mgmt_mid",
      q_occ_current_raw %in% top_management_vec ~ "mgmt_top",
      q_occ_current_raw %in% shop_owner_vec ~ "owner_shop",
      q_occ_current_raw %in% business_owner_vec ~ "owner_biz",
      q_occ_current_raw %in% self_employed_prof_vec ~ "prof_self",
      q_occ_current_raw %in% employed_prof_vec ~ "prof_emp",
      .default = NA_character_
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: occ-validate

  filter(is.na(q_occ_current) & !is.na(q_occ_current_raw)) |>
  count(q_occ_current_raw)
```

```{r}
      .default = NA_character_
    )
```

## Meta Country Raw

character variable, encodes the country from which respondent participated

## Meta psid

[Dynata Identifier Help Page](__https://help.dynata.com/s/article/Identifier-9cc7c84a__) describes `psid` as the **Session ID** — a unique identifier for a panelist *within a single survey*. Each time a panelist enters a survey, they receive a new `psid`. It identifies one survey-taking event (panelist × survey-entry), not the person.

## Meta pid

The `pid` is the **Panelist ID** — a unique and static identifier for a panelist across *all* surveys launched with Dynata. The same person carries the same `pid` from survey to survey and wave to wave, making it the correct key for tracking respondents across waves of a panel study.

**Relationship:** `pid` ⊃ `psid` ⊃ `responseid`. In the stacked EU25 data, 78,060 unique `pid`s produced 102,766 unique `psid`s (~1.32 sessions per panelist, reflecting repeat participation across waves) and 103,685 raw response rows (~900 rows beyond unique sessions, indicating some `psid`s have multiple records — likely re-entries, partial+complete pairs, or duplicate exports worth checking before treating one row as one observation).

## Meta device

empty variable, can be dropped later

```{r}
#| label: recode-q_religion
.norm <- function(x) stringi::stri_trans_nfc(trimws(x))
df_stacked_recoded <- df_stacked_recoded |>
  mutate(
    .q_rel = .norm(q_religion_raw),
    q_religion = case_when(
      .q_rel %in% .norm(catholic_vec) ~ "catholic",
      .q_rel %in% .norm(protestant_vec) ~ "protestant",
      .q_rel %in% .norm(orthodox_vec) ~ "orthodox",
      .q_rel %in% .norm(other_christian_vec) ~ "other_christian",
      .q_rel %in% .norm(muslim_vec) ~ "muslim",
      .q_rel %in% .norm(jewish_vec) ~ "jewish",
      .q_rel %in% .norm(buddhist_vec) ~ "buddhist",
      .q_rel %in% .norm(hindu_vec) ~ "hindu",
      .q_rel %in% .norm(sikh_vec) ~ "sikh",
      .q_rel %in% .norm(atheist_vec) ~ "atheist",
      .q_rel %in% .norm(nonbeliever_agnostic_vec) ~ "nonbeliever_agnostic",
      .q_rel %in% .norm(other_religion_vec) ~ "other",
      .q_rel %in% .norm(dont_know_vec) ~ "dont_know",
      .default = NA_character_
    ),
    .q_rel = NULL
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: recode-q_class
df_stacked_recoded <- df_stacked_recoded |>
  mutate(
    q_class = case_when(
      q_class_raw %in% working_class_vec ~ "working_class",
      q_class_raw %in% lower_middle_class_vec ~ "lower_middle_class",
      q_class_raw %in% middle_class_vec ~ "middle_class",
      q_class_raw %in% upper_middle_class_vec ~ "upper_middle_class",
      q_class_raw %in% higher_class_vec ~ "higher_class",
      q_class_raw %in% other_class_vec ~ "other",
      q_class_raw %in% dont_know_vec ~ "dont_know",
      .default = NA_character_
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: validate-q_class
df_stacked_recoded |>
  select(q_class, q_class_raw) |>
  filter(is.na(q_class) & !is.na(q_class_raw)) |>
  distinct(q_class_raw) |>
  print(n = 100)
```

```{r}
#| label: eu-int-pos-recode
df_stacked_recoded <- df_stacked_recoded |>
  mutate(
    q_euint_pos = case_when(
      str_detect(q_euint_pos_raw, "^\\(1\\)") ~ 1L,
      str_detect(q_euint_pos_raw, "^\\(2\\)") ~ 2L,
      str_detect(q_euint_pos_raw, "^\\(3\\)") ~ 3L,
      str_detect(q_euint_pos_raw, "^\\(4\\)") ~ 4L,
      str_detect(q_euint_pos_raw, "^\\(5\\)") ~ 5L,
      str_detect(q_euint_pos_raw, "^\\(6\\)") ~ 6L,
      str_detect(q_euint_pos_raw, "^\\(7\\)") ~ 7L,
      TRUE ~ NA_integer_
    )
  )
```

## Vote and other Variables containing party values
 

### Identify party-bearing variables {#sec-party-vars-identify}

Variables holding party-name values, confirmed for Party Facts harmonization.
Scale placements (`q_lr_party_*`, `q_euint_party_*`), thermometer ratings (`q_thermo_*_raw`), conjoint policy-position strings (`cj_rand_party_*`), rank numbers (`q_vote_exp_rank_party_*`), turnout (`q_vote_eu_2014_raw`) and the attachment scale (`q_party_closeness_raw`) are excluded because they do not contain party names.

### Thermometer party crosswalk {#sec-party-vars-thermo}

The party rated in each `q_thermo_N_raw` slot is country-specific and lives only in the `Q196_*` question wording, not in a respondent column.
The slot to `Q196_*` mapping is transcribed from the wave-cleaning notebooks (`04_clean_w2`, `05_clean_w3`; identical across waves), then joined to the wording lookup to recover the party shown in each slot.

```{r}
#| label: party-vars-thermo-crosswalk
wording_map <- read_csv(
  here("data", "02_processed", "question_wording_map.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

thermo_groupA <- c(
  "Austria",
  "Belgium",
  "Croatia",
  "Czechia",
  "Estonia",
  "Finland",
  "France",
  "Greece",
  "Italy",
  "Latvia",
  "Slovakia",
  "Slovenia",
  "Spain",
  "Sweden"
)
thermo_groupB <- c(
  "Bulgaria",
  "Denmark",
  "Hungary",
  "Lithuania",
  "Netherlands",
  "Poland",
  "United Kingdom"
)

thermo_slot_codes <- function(country) {
  rest <- if (country %in% thermo_groupA) {
    17:21
  } else if (country %in% thermo_groupB) {
    12:16
  } else if (country == "Germany") {
    22:26
  } else if (country == "Ireland") {
    7:11
  } else if (country == "Portugal") {
    27:31
  } else if (country == "Romania") {
    18:22
  } else {
    return(rep(NA_character_, 6))
  }
  c("Q196_1", paste0("Q196_", rest))
}

# longest common prefix of a character vector (the shared question instruction)
lcp <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) {
    return("")
  }
  chars <- strsplit(x, "")
  n <- min(lengths(chars))
  out <- ""
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    ci <- unique(map_chr(chars, i))
    if (length(ci) == 1L) out <- paste0(out, ci) else break
  }
  out
}

thermo_party_map <- map(sort(unique(wording_map$country)), function(ct) {
  tibble(meta_country = ct, thermo_slot = 1:6, col_name = thermo_slot_codes(ct))
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  crossing(wave = c(2, 3)) |>
  left_join(
    wording_map,
    by = c("wave", "meta_country" = "country", "col_name")
  ) |>
  # party = wording suffix after the LAST " - " inside the common instruction
  # prefix (hyphen-safe: keeps party names that themselves contain " - ")
  group_by(wave, meta_country) |>
  mutate(
    .cp = lcp(wording),
    .sep_end = {
      pos <- str_locate_all(.cp, fixed(" - "))[[1]]
      if (nrow(pos) == 0) 0L else pos[nrow(pos), "end"]
    },
    party_spelling = str_trim(str_sub(wording, .sep_end + 1))
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(wave, meta_country, thermo_slot, party_spelling)

thermo_party_map
```

### Collect distinct spellings {#sec-party-vars-collect}

Stack the distinct `meta_country` x `party_spelling` combinations per source variable, then split closed-list from open-end fields and write both to disk as the input for the `party_recode_map` crosswalk.

```{r}
#| label: party-vars-collect-spellings
party_list_for_stacking <- map(
  party_vars,
  ~ {
    var_symbol <- sym(.x)
    df_stacked |>
      group_by(meta_country) |>
      select(meta_country, {{ var_symbol }}) |>
      distinct() |>
      rename(party_spelling = {{ var_symbol }}) |>
      mutate(source_variable = .x) |>
      ungroup()
  }
)

parties_for_recode <- party_list_for_stacking |>
  list_rbind() |>
  filter(!is.na(party_spelling) & party_spelling != "") |>
  arrange(meta_country, party_spelling, source_variable) |>
  distinct()

# thermometer party labels (country-level constants) enter as a closed-list source
parties_thermo <- thermo_party_map |>
  distinct(meta_country, party_spelling) |>
  filter(!is.na(party_spelling) & party_spelling != "") |>
  mutate(source_variable = "q_thermo_party")

parties_for_recode <- parties_for_recode |>
  bind_rows(parties_thermo) |>
  arrange(meta_country, party_spelling, source_variable) |>
  distinct()

parties_for_recode_openend <- parties_for_recode |>
  filter(str_detect(source_variable, "other|text"))

parties_for_recode_closed <- parties_for_recode |>
  filter(!str_detect(source_variable, "other|text"))

write_csv(
  parties_for_recode_closed,
  here("data", "02_processed", "parties_for_recode_closed.csv")
)
write_csv(
  parties_for_recode_openend,
  here("data", "02_processed", "parties_for_recode_openend.csv")
)

parties_for_recode |>
  count(source_variable, name = "n_spellings") |>
  arrange(desc(n_spellings))
```

### Party Facts crosswalk {#sec-party-recode-map}

Paste the populated `party_recode_map` tribble into a chunk labelled `party-recode-map` directly below (schema `~meta_country, ~party_spelling, ~pf_name, ~pf_id`; one shared map joined against every variable, no `source_variable` column).

The crosswalk codes Czech parties under `meta_country == "Czech Republic"`, but the survey data uses `"Czechia"`; align the two so the Czech rows match.

```{r}
#| label: party-recode-map-fix
party_recode_map <- party_recode_map |>
  mutate(
    meta_country = if_else(
      meta_country == "Czech Republic",
      "Czechia",
      meta_country
    )
  )
```

Spelling / format variants and response options found in this dataset but missing from the crosswalk above.
Real parties reuse the `pf_name` / `pf_id` of their canonical match; parties absent from Party Facts take `"<name> [og]"` with `NA`; non-party responses get a harmonized English category label (`none`, `dont-know`, `did-not-vote`, `will-not-vote`, `not-eligible`, `other`, `other-country`) with `NA` id.
`will-not-vote` (future-tense abstention in the vote-intention items) and `other-country` (respondent votes in another country) are added on top of the old notebook's category set.

```{r}
party_recode_map <- bind_rows(party_recode_map, party_recode_map_ext)
```

Open-end ("Other, specify") and free-text responses (recurring values, n >= 2).
Matching is case-insensitive, so one representative spelling per concept covers its case variants.
Recognized parties take their `pf_name` / `pf_id` (or `"<name> [og]"` when absent from Party Facts); protest / non-disclosure responses take a category label with `NA` id.
Category labels extend the earlier set with `blank-invalid` (blank or spoilt ballot), `refused` (declines to disclose / secret ballot), and `independent` (independent candidate).
Individual candidates' names and gibberish are left to fall through to `NA`.

### Join Party Facts ids {#sec-party-recode-join}

Join the shared crosswalk onto each party-name variable, adding `ext_<var>_pf_name` / `ext_<var>_pf_id` siblings (raw columns untouched).
The thermometer party shown in each slot is matched per `(meta_wave, meta_country)` via `thermo_party_map`.

```{r}
#| label: party-recode-join
# match on a normalized key: collapse runs of whitespace and fold Unicode line/
# paragraph separators and non-breaking spaces to a single space, so trailing /
# double-space /  spelling variants match without enumerating each one
norm_key <- function(x) {
  x |>
    str_replace_all("[ ]", " ") |>
    str_squish() |>
    str_to_lower()
}

map_join <- party_recode_map |>
  transmute(
    meta_country,
    join_key = norm_key(party_spelling),
    pf_name,
    pf_id
  ) |>
  distinct()

# a normalized key must map to a single pf within a country, else the left_join
# would multiply rows
stopifnot(max(count(map_join, meta_country, join_key)$n) == 1)

party_vars_to_join <- c(party_vars_closed, party_vars_openend)

df_stacked_recoded <- reduce(
  party_vars_to_join,
  function(df, var) {
    stub <- str_remove(var, "_raw")
    df |>
      mutate(.join_key = norm_key(.data[[var]])) |>
      left_join(map_join, by = c("meta_country", ".join_key" = "join_key")) |>
      select(-.join_key) |>
      rename(
        !!paste0("ext_", stub, "_pf_name") := pf_name,
        !!paste0("ext_", stub, "_pf_id") := pf_id
      )
  },
  .init = df_stacked_recoded
)

# thermometer: party shown per (wave, country, slot) -> pf via the shared map
thermo_pf <- thermo_party_map |>
  mutate(join_key = norm_key(party_spelling)) |>
  left_join(map_join, by = c("meta_country", "join_key")) |>
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(wave, meta_country),
    names_from = thermo_slot,
    values_from = c(pf_name, pf_id),
    names_glue = "ext_q_thermo_{thermo_slot}_{.value}"
  )

df_stacked_recoded <- df_stacked_recoded |>
  left_join(thermo_pf, by = c("meta_wave" = "wave", "meta_country"))
```

### Validate Party Facts join {#sec-party-recode-validate}

For each variable, list spellings that are non-missing but received no `pf_name` (unmatched in the crosswalk).
A clean result is no output beyond legitimate gaps.

```{r}
#| label: party-recode-validate
walk(c(party_vars_closed, party_vars_openend), function(var) {
  pf <- paste0("ext_", str_remove(var, "_raw"), "_pf_name")
  unmatched <- df_stacked_recoded |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[var]]) & .data[[var]] != "" & is.na(.data[[pf]])) |>
    count(meta_country, .data[[var]], sort = TRUE)
  if (nrow(unmatched) > 0) {
    cat("\n--- unmatched:", var, "(", nrow(unmatched), "spellings ) ---\n")
    print(unmatched, n = 25)
  }
})

# thermometer slots with no Party Facts match
thermo_party_map |>
  left_join(
    party_recode_map |> select(meta_country, party_spelling, pf_id),
    by = c("meta_country", "party_spelling")
  ) |>
  filter(is.na(pf_id)) |>
  distinct(meta_country, party_spelling)
```

```{r}
      q_news_tv_raw %in% never_vec ~ "never",

      q_news_tv_raw %in% several_pw_vec ~ "several_pw",
      q_news_tv_raw %in% almost_every_day_vec ~ "almost_every_day",
      q_news_tv_raw %in% every_day_vec ~ "every_day",
      .default = NA_character_
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: recode-news_tv_days
df_stacked_recoded <- df_stacked_recoded |>

    q_news_tv_days = case_when(
      q_news_tv_days_raw %in% less_than_1_day_vec ~ 0L,

      q_news_tv_days_raw %in% days_6_vec ~ 6L,
      q_news_tv_days_raw %in% days_7_vec ~ 7L,
      .default = NA_integer_
    )
  )
```
